title: Descent of complete-intersection residue fibres on a chosen affine chart
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ be affine opens with $f(U)\subseteq V$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime. Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $S=B\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and assume that $S$ is a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $k\to K$ be any extension of fields, and let $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ be the composite $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k\to V\to Y$. Write $X_K=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $\pi:X_K\to X$ for the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $X_K$ has an affine open cover by spectra of finite type $K$-algebras that are local complete intersections over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is affine, and there are $K$-scheme and $K$-algebra isomorphisms
$$\pi^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A K),\qquad \alpha:S\otimes_kK\xrightarrow{\sim} B\otimes_A K.$$
The first isomorphism identifies the maps to $U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K$ with the spectrum maps of $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $u\mapsto1\otimes u$, respectively; the algebra isomorphism satisfies $\alpha((b\otimes c)\otimes u)=b\otimes cu$ and $\alpha^{-1}(b\otimes u)=(b\otimes1)\otimes u$. The algebras $B\otimes_A K$ over $K$ and $S$ over $k$ are local complete intersections. No flatness, finite presentation of $f$, algebraicity of $K/k$, or algebraic closedness of $K$ is assumed. Empty opens, empty fibres and zero fibre algebras are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), descent/ascent; schemes.tex Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product) and 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); morphisms.tex Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection). Explicit affine-chart and balanced-tensor comparison extracted from the proof of lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion, original steps 1, 3 and 6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to $X\to Y$, $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ and the opens $U\subset X$, $V\subset Y$, $\operatorname{Spec}K\subset\operatorname{Spec}K$. Both maps land in $V$ by hypothesis. It identifies $W=\pi^{-1}(U)$ with $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$, compatibly with both projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ the restriction $U\to V$ of $f$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the induced map $A\to B$, and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $A\to k\to K$ by construction. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], this is $\operatorname{Spec}D$ for $D=B\otimes_AK$, with the projections induced by $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $u\mapsto1\otimes u$. Thus $W$ is affine and the comparison is over $K$.

Write $i:k\to K$ for the given embedding and $\bar a$ for the image of $a\in A$ in $k$. The maps $B\to D$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and $k\to D$, $c\mapsto1\otimes i(c)$, agree on $A$: $a_B\otimes1=1\otimes i(\bar a)$. The tensor pushout property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $h:S\to D$ with $h(b\otimes c)=b\otimes i(c)$. This is a $k$-algebra map, so the same property with $S$ and $K$ over $k$ gives a $K$-algebra map $\alpha:S\otimes_kK\to D$ satisfying $\alpha((b\otimes c)\otimes u)=b\otimes i(c)u$. Conversely the maps $B\to S\otimes_kK$, $b\mapsto(b\otimes1)\otimes1$, and $K\to S\otimes_kK$, $u\mapsto1_S\otimes u$, agree on $A$, since $(a_B\otimes1)\otimes1=(1\otimes\bar a)\otimes1=(1\otimes1)\otimes i(\bar a)$. The pushout property over $A$ therefore gives a $K$-algebra map $\beta:D\to S\otimes_kK$ with $\beta(b\otimes u)=(b\otimes1)\otimes u$.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), proof: the Hom-of-tensor-product universal-property formula; explicit balanced-tensor calculation by Q94.

proof.text: On pure tensors $\alpha\beta(b\otimes u)=b\otimes u$ and $\beta\alpha((b\otimes c)\otimes u)=(b\otimes1)\otimes i(c)u=(b\otimes c)\otimes u$. The last equality is the $k$-balancing relation. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], first for $B\otimes_Ak$ and then for its tensor product with $K$, makes these identities equalities of homomorphisms. Thus $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), proof: the Hom-of-tensor-product universal-property formula; explicit balanced-tensor calculation by Q94.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-lci-affine-open-locality] with base field $K$, scheme $Z=X_K$ and affine open $W$. Its cover hypothesis is exactly the assumed cover of $X_K$ by finite type local-complete-intersection $K$-algebras. Hence $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ is finite type and a local complete intersection over $K$. The projection-compatible affine comparison of step 1 identifies this coordinate algebra with $D$ as a $K$-algebra, so $D$ has these properties.

The complete-intersection definition [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] is invariant under a base-field algebra isomorphism: carry a principal cover $D(g_j)$ to the cover $D(e(g_j))$; the isomorphism induces isomorphisms of the localizations, and compose each polynomial-quotient presentation with these isomorphisms. Krull dimensions agree because the corresponding spectra are homeomorphic. Finite generation is carried by the images of a finite set of generators. Apply this observation to $\alpha^{-1}:D\cong S\otimes_kK$ to obtain that $S\otimes_kK$ is a local complete intersection over $K$.

source.place: Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), invariance of the defining presentations and principal-open covers under algebra isomorphism.

proof.text: Now [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change] applies to the given field extension $k\to K$ and the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ (finite type is an explicit hypothesis of the item). Its reverse implication, using step 5, gives that $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$. Step 4 already gives the assertion for $D$. All formulas and universal-property arguments allow zero algebras; for the empty open the locality lemma explicitly includes the zero coordinate algebra. None of these steps requires flatness or finite presentation of $f$, or algebraicity or algebraic closedness of $K$.
